main_result: At microscopic scaling of Haar U(N), a Schwartz test with Fourier support in [−2/m,2/m] gives first m Gaussian moments, with the indicated mean and variance. The paper attributes a balanced Fourier cumulant vanishing range to Soshnikov and proves parallel results for Sp(N) and SO(N).

main_result: For even real f with smooth compactly supported Fourier transform, centers continuously averaged near T on scale T^a, 0<a≤1, against a nonnegative normalized Schwartz weight with compact Fourier support, have first m local zero-statistic moments asymptotically Gaussian when Fourier support is in (−2a/m,2a/m). No RH assumption. The Schwartz decay qualification repairs the literal omission of tail control in the source.
read_scope: All four journal pages read. Compared the statement and prime-power argument with the longer arXiv v1 at Theorems 1.1 and 2.6.
result_status: Source theorem with a tail-decay qualification. The accompanying audit gives a counterexample to the literal weight scope and checks the sufficient Schwartz setting. No canonical error adjudication.
selection_reason: The explicit formula contains the same prime logarithmic frequency but the theorem uses a different sampling law and smooth cutoff.
title: Linear statistics for zeros of Riemann’s zeta function
transfer_hypothesis: The explicit formula contains the same prime logarithmic frequency but the theorem uses a different sampling law and smooth cutoff.

main_result: The Fourier transform of a multivariate nonnegative polynomial times a nonsingular normal density is a polynomial times its normal transform. If such a product is a characteristic function, the inverse has the stated polynomial-normal density.
read_scope: Targeted source reading of the definition and transform equivalence. Main decomposition proof unextracted.
result_status: Source-stated scoped result. No derivative-weighted arithmetic transfer is established by this source.
selection_reason: Standard transform antecedent for testing a formal arithmetic Gaussian-polynomial continuation for positivity. Positive definiteness is a hypothesis of the converse.
